Title: Document 5b
Content: The Members of Congress and distinguished guests, my fellow Americans, we gather here today to right a grave wrong. More than `text(40 years)` ago, shortly after the bombing of Pearl Harbor, `text(120,000)` persons of Japanese ancestry living in the United States were forcibly removed from their homes and placed in makeshift internment camps. This action was taken without trial, without jury. It was based solely on race, for these `text(120,000)` were Americans of Japanese descent...

The legislation that I am about to sign provides for a restitution payment to each of the `text(60,000)` surviving Japanese-Americans of the `text(120,000)` who were relocated or detained. Yet no payment can make up for those lost `text(years)`. So, what is most important in this bill has less to do with property than with honor. For here we admit a wrong; here we reaffirm our commitment as a nation to equal justice under the law.
